Other members in my party did not enjoy their ice creams either. However, they did maintain a clean area and provided hand sanitizers which I liked, especially during times like these.

I really like the pizza and veggie options at Fino's and have been trying to support them by ordering more often since the pandemic started. That said, I was disappointed when I arrived recently to pick up my order and the men working inside were not wearing masks. The owner has always been really friendly and I want to support them, but I feel like I can't do that safely until they change this practice for the benefit of their customers.

Did the walk up window and placed an order for 4 bagel sandwiches. I was surprised at how busy this spot was for a weekday. Lots of people picking up orders. Which I do recommend call ahead just because we did wait about 20 minutes for our order by just walking up. We got a pretzel bagel, pumpernickel, everything and plain. All the bagels were good. All but 1 with scrabbled eggs. The other was a fried egg that was over cooked. I think it was probably ok when it first came out but Bc they wrapped it all up to go it continued to cook and be over cooked. Overall we were all satisfied with the bagels. They were good and chewy. The pretzel bagel with bacon and cheese ate a bit salty but I think that was Bc of the salty nature of bacon and cheese and more of me ordering issue then a them issue. In our 3 days in town we ate here twice. Would recommend.

I came here based on a book called "Unique Eats and Eateries" written by Irene Levy Baker.  The restaurant is in the basement of building that also houses a piano bar and a dance floor, but both were not in operation when my wife and I dined here on a Thursday night.  

We were one of two tables and the service was fast and efficient.  They have a full page selection of craft beer and wines at fair prices.  The menu is simple, and with some research before we went, we ordered the fries (amazing), cheese sandwich with tomato soup, and the Wedge Salad.  All of the food was perfectly cooked and had great taste.  The fries were as good as you can make them.  The wedge needed a little more Blue Cheese which the server immediately brought.  

I highly recommend the Tavern as a great place to eat in Center City.

Ordered delivery here and was genuinely impressed. I am confused as to why I haven't tried this place sooner. They have a vast assortment of sides & dishes, I tried the pork buns which were amazingly fluffy with a spicy slaw, the wings were half spicy & half soy garlic and let me tell you that if you love spice, the spicy wings will NOT disappoint. The chicken was marvelously crunchy with plenty of meat. Next the fried pickles were good (how can you mess up a fried pickle?!), again, the spicy ranch / mayo paired excellent with those. Now I wasn't quite sure about the fried rice when I opened the container but upon my first bite I was hit with flavor and possibly my favorite thing here. Can't wait to order again & try more things! (Also, portions are huge and there was plenty left over after sharing this with my partner!)
Excellent food especially the Indian menu !! Would order 30 minutes ahead of pick up and eat at home rather than at the joint!!

I have three words for you that will change your life:

The Pastrami Reuben.

That's it. That's all you need. Whether it's a bad day and you need a pick me up or a good day and you need to make it better, just get the pastrami Reuben and all your problems in life will suddenly disappear for the 15-30 mins it will take to eat your sandwich. I'm fortunate that I can't normally eat the whole thing in one day so I get to eat it again the next day and it tastes even better. If you're in Philadelphia, eating this is a must. Just saying. Don't leave without eating here, you will regret it.

Used DoorDash to have my protein bowl delivered for lunch. Extremely filling and delicious! Perfect meal for lunch. Portion size was perfect and the bowl was very generous with the chicken, avocado, eggs, etc. no complaints with my food and I will be back!

The food was awesome but some things were okay. Overall this place had great drinks and food, but I would've loved a better atmosphere. Music was great! We were hoping to get the special of the day, but I guess it wasn't there anymore. We were bummed about that.

My favorite sushi place in Philly. Whats truly stunning is that I don't even come here for their fish, I crave this place for their INCREDIBLE vegetarian sushi. 

They're extremely creative with their various vegan specialty rolls. You can't go wrong with any of them but some of my favorites are the lime sinko, veggie tomo, and vegan dragon rolls. They also have great appetizer buns and fish forward sushi.

Highly recommended.

I dined with three friends on Friday evening.  We didn't get to dine in the garden but the structure they built along the sidewalk was fine. The food amazing especially the short rib and the creme brûlée. This restaurant never disappoints!

If you are looking for outstanding service and a professional cut check out Max and staff. It's a safe and friendly place to get your hair styled however you like. Support this business and I'm sure you will be pleased.

I love winnies for breakfast/brunch, but came here for a very late lunch for the first time today. The lunch menu did not disappoint at all! I ordered the salmon burger, which was amazing with that ginger/cucumber. My bf ordered the fried chicken sandwich, which was absolutely delicious. I think I preferred his over mine. I also devoured the house chips that came with my meal. Definitely coming back

The barbecue made noises, and a drop of hot oil slowly slid down the lines of the plump meat, which was intoxicating.  Sniffing and smelling slowly, the greedy worms are quickly aroused.  Finally couldn't help it, regardless of the hot, one bite is a big bite.

This jawn bussin. 

This place is absolutely amazing, it may be pricey but it's worth your time. There's so much food to choose from and it comes out super fast ! It's an experience you never experienced while eating Korean food. Totally recommend coming here after a long day. Make sure to bring your family along for the experience !

If I could give this place 10 stars I would! It is one of my favorite vegan spots. Their new outdoor booths are quaint and cute too! Try their Mexican hot chocolate it's so tasty. I've only gone here post brunch but anyone I've gone here with loves (both vegan/non vegan). You really can't tell the difference with the food. It's high quality and tasty. The staff members are great too. I'm not a drinker (of alcohol lol) but they have a full bar with many drinks. So you could come here for a date night or just a bar night! My goal is to try everything on the menu...but it's hard to go here and 'not' order the nachos because they are sooooo good.
When I lost my card, I called to cancel. However, they did not really cancel it, and so someone used it again!!! Is it not policy to cancel a card if it is reported lost and stolen?

I love botanical gardens: The Brooklyn, The New York, The Phipps in Pittsburgh, even the Desert Botanical Garden in Phoenix. 
I went to the Philadelphia Garden Show with high hopes. 
To say I was severely disappointed is an understatement. 

It was basically an advertisement for flower vendors with designs that were not especially attractive or imaginative, with too many booths selling knick knacks. 

I can't think of a bigger waste of more than forty dollars. I can't understand how they survive: PT Barnum said there's a sucker born every minute. Today it was me. 

I just got home but felt a civic responsibility to try to dissuade as many people as possible from wasting $48 and several hours of their life this weekend at this overpriced, underwhelming show. 

There are many excellent ways to spend several hours in Philadelphia: It has one of the greatest art museums, not just in the country, but the world. Four sports teams, with vocal and knowledgeable fans,  play in stadiums and arenas in the southern part of the city; there is Independence Hall, where our country was born, and you cannot get a bad Italian meal anywhere in town. 

But the Flower Show? If it were a movie, it would be a scene from 'Rocky' where Paulie scratches his crotch.

No I am a very picky picky picky picky picky eater! But this place was amazing!!! I had an amazing piece of toast with sweet potatoes and it was something like I never experienced. I thought I'd hate it, but low and behold here I am ranting and raving lol I had the jerk chicken as my meal and my date had cod and it was also great. The drinks were delicious too! I felt comfortable. All the staff members wore mask I was seated outside just before the weather really broke as I only wore that sweater in the picture. There were also plastic dividers and no one sitting on either side of you directly a mini booth over for everyone.
$20.50 for barely a pound of roasted pork in a take-out plastic container is ridiculous.  It didn't taste that great either.

This place was horrible, the bartenders were lazy and only paid attention to their friends, the DJ cleared the room with bad music.... I want to like this place but it's hard when I'm waiting 8 mins to get my card back while I'm watching the bartender talk to her friend in the corner

Joe and his team were very helpful.  I had a variety of items that I wanted to get rid of - an old gas grill, old patio furniture, a TV.  He answered my email within hours and worked with my schedule to figure out a time to come haul everything away.  Great service and totally reasonable price.  Very nice man and great service
Their platters are the absolute best! The food is excellent and always consistent. Very happy customer!

This is one of my favorite places to visit in Philly. For the past five years, I have brought a high school Model UN team to a conference in Old City, and I walk to this market at least once each day we are here. The food options are amazing: I always visit Bieler's stalls (doughnuts and baked goods), and I get breakfast most mornings at Miller's Twists (pretzel-wrapped egg sandwiches). There are bakeries, delis, gift shops, chocolatiers, ethnic food kiosks, and coffee stands--and more. Even the pickiest eater will find something here to enjoy.
Good food, good vibes. Will definitely re-visit. Everything we ordered was delicious.

Fantastic hotel - restaurant food is way better than most hotels and bar staff is pleasantly helpful.   It's been weird since COVID - but so glad they held it together a I have stayed there many times over the years when I was going to Grad school across the street and now stay there cause our daughter is full-time at Penn.   Super quiet rooms abs very clean - also has a nice clean gym too!

Phenomenal! Catered a party of approximately 40 for a graduation. Everyone asked for Bacchus' name. Fresh tuna with a wasabi sauce, delicious light vegetarian or cheesesteak egg rolls. Summer corn salad. Noodles with a light peanut sauce which did not overwhelm. Guests of all ages enjoyed.

4 Stars because 95% Of the time I go there and get the GENRAL TSO style chicken it is good, sometimes they might fry it too hard without you requesting that and it becomes chewy and hard to eat ( Just make sure you let them k ow you don't want that ) But other than that if your in the Juanita/northeast philly area looking for GENRAL TSO chicken I recommend LUNS ASAIN CHEF

We tried both Geno's and Pat's side by side, and they were both quite tasty. I ordered a cheesesteak whiz wit. Geno's cheeze-whiz sauce was a lot thinner and wetter, I would have liked the the onions cooked a bit more, but I definitely prefer Geno's steak and bread. The steak is more tender and I believe has better flavor. Geno's bread seems to hold up better, but then again that could be due to the fact that they didn't use as much cheese. PleasI'm sure there are better and cheaper cheesesteaks in Philly, but we had to try the touristy places first.

First, so delicious!! 

Second, the food was super hot when I picked it up which meant it was warm enough to eat without reheating when I got home (about a 50-minute drive). 

Third, it tasted like home cooking. 

Finally, my semi-picky eater child declared it was the best meal ever (I tried to not take it personally...lol). 

Dinner was done in 5 minutes because everyone ate so fast!

I stopped in for lunch yesterday, around 2p, so it appeared that I missed the lunch rush, so there was no line. I had spring mix/brown rice as the base, carrots and Mac & cheese as sides, charred chicken thigh was my protein choice. Everything was absolutely delicious! I plan to pick up takeout for tonight's dinner!

This is without a doubt the best Indian restaurant in West Philly. Everything we tried, from the appetizers to the curries and Naan bread, was excellent. The restaurant is beautiful on the inside and the service was great. Highly recommended!
Food was good and server was very nice and  friendly ! I definitely recommend for a date night !

I heard about Paddywax while searching for offbeat activities in Philadelphia. I quickly made a reservation for two people ($40 per person). These classes seem to sell out so I wouldn't recommend walking in with no reservation. 

Upon walking in I have to say I was a bit overwhelmed by the smell. I did get used to it, but I wouldn't recommend remaining in the store for those with sensitive smell. 

They have coffee, soft drinks and some alcoholic beverages (like white claw) for purchase. Or you can bring your own wine or champagne. Most I saw brought Champagne or Wine. 

It is not a complicated process and everyone including the mildly intoxicated will get through it with a beautiful candle. I went with my boyfriend and had a great time, but I do believe going with a group of girlfriends would have been a bit more fun. May be more appreciative of it, but he used the time to make a Mother's Day gift for his mom. 

It is a bit pricey, but I agree with the first reviewer, you get a bit of a price inflate for being on chestnut street. It's a very good location I must say and there is plenty to do while you wait for your candle to cure. 

The Process: 

1. Pick your vessel
2. Pick your Fragrance (there were only certain amounts of fragrances available. So if someone nabbed it first, you must choose a different one).
3. Put cotton or wooden wick at base of your vessel. 
4. You use your scale and weigh out the amount of fragrance for your candle. All in a little booklet provided to you.
5. Weigh the amount of wax needed. Again don't fret, it's all in the booklet. 
6. Mix the fragrance and wax together for 20 seconds.
7. Pour into candle vessel.
8. Use tool to keep wick in proper place. 
9. Whaala, you have yourself a new candle made and poured by you!
10. It must sit and cure for 3 hours.
Superb! More crab than I have ever eaten in 1 setting. Also, the best dumplings of life. Will return!!!!

All the reviews are spot on. Chris is a patient, conscientious, well educated teacher who knows how to break down each part of your swing and explain the kinesiology of golf. Not only is he renown for his understanding or the mechanics and ability to teach PGA professionals, but he's also a very real and personable guy. He makes the experience more than just a golf lesson. I wanted to learn golfing for my husband but he's transformed not just the way I want to play golf but also the dynamics for how to play confidently in different types of scenarios. I highly recommend him.

I love it here!!! They are a big family that treats their customers like family. I love it here! Everyone always treats me like a cool guy. Alicia, Lynn, and Donna are my favorites!!! Alicia and Lynn always have my back!!! I love you all and please keep up the good work! I'll always be a regular here! Donna, you have a great family. -Dennis
Really like the decor and the beer selection, however the food was not good at all.  The fries were undercooked and the Shepard's  Pie was a multi layer concoction of blandness.

I really enjoyed my Mother's Day Soul Fed Sunday meal. We drove in from Delaware and it was well worth it. Oh I cannot forget to mention the Po' Boy sandwiches. I think I visited Heaven it was that delightful. You can't go wrong with anything you order.

Such a great bakery. I have been here pre and post pandemic 4 or 5 times and have also had their pastries at my office. The bakery is fairly small with a couple of seats and just enough room for a few people to stand in line. The workers are so sweet and clearly excited to share their love of pastries with the masses.

I have had the chocolate chip cookie, Brookie, chocolate fudge brownie, oat walnut brownie, blueberry swirl muffin, chocolate Nutella muffin, coffee cake, chocolate chip scone and maple oat scone. All phenomenal. 

I tend to frequently enjoy the Nutella Muffin, Brookie, and Chocolate Chip Scone. My least favorite is the maple oat scone because it is made with shredded coconut which I don't prefer.

I need to wake up earlier because the babkas sell out instantly and I have yet to try it. One day. Either way I'm just as content consuming whatever they have left once I mosey on in during the late afternoon.

Came here a week ago with a few friends and it was some of the best hot pot I've ever had in my life. Everything from the sauces, soup, and meat was delicious. Our server, Dean was excellent -- he constantly checked on us and gave us great recommendations on the menu. Will definitely be back soon.
Initially responded with a quote and then completely disappeared. Disappointing and frustrating to just be ignored when trying to give someone work.

I was turned on to Steven Singer by a co-worker from Philly (he and I were working in California at the time). I've been hooked on their dipped roses as a regular Valentines Day gift for my wife!

This year, I was indecisive (being a typical "guy" at Valentines Day). I was LUCKY to call and reach Krista at the store!  Not only was she bright and friendly ... she was BEYOND helpful!  I was stuck on which dipped rose to buy, and based on my order history, she helped me decide on the right one for this year.  Additionally, when I had writers block for the gift note, she helped write it the way she'd want to receive it.  Krista provided such great service, she up sold me in a second on some add-ons that totally complete the gift for this year!

Krista not only provided great service, but it was an outstanding purchase experience!  Looking forward to maintaining my loyalty to this business, (which I have never even stepped in).  Their online service is epic, and the next time I'm in Philly, I plan to give a sincere thanks to their entire team!  Thank you Krista and Steven Singer. Despite their name, I truly do LOVE (and recommend) Steven Singer Jewelers!
Warm, friendly owners who greet you with a smile.  I've had the shawarma, gyro and falafel sandwiches.  All are equally delicious.  My go-to when I visit the area.

I came here for a post Covid event on a Friday evening.  I believe sip city mixer was a private happy hour event so my review is strictly on the location as I did not dine at Cavanaugh'a riverdeck.

The Riverdeck's entrance is easy to spot and getting in through security was easy once we showed IDs.  They had a tent set up and there were 3 bars within the outside area, each in a different section of the facility.  There was a lot of people and everyone now being maskless including the bartender takes some getting used to.  The view was okay and I had a good time.

After constantly passing Nook on our walk home, my boyfriend and I finally stopped by after our workout. We usually go to the Starbucks just a few steps away.... We have already gone to Nook twice in three days. 

My boyfriend said it was the best Pumpkin Spice Latte that he's ever had - (and we LOVE that we can still get our favorite flavor in February). 

They are sustainably sourced and make their own coffee. LOVE THAT - but to make things better, the workers couldn't be sweeter either.

Definitely give Nook a try - you will not be disappointed.

Excellent deli.  Very good hoagies.  I love the fact that they carry all kinds of Italian meats since I love cooking Italian.  The prosciutto that you find in the supermarket is most definitely not the same quality as Dattilo's carries. Same with their rolls.  They're the right kind of roll.  Hard outside, soft inner.  Philadelphians know the difference, but supermarkets just don't get that.  They carry all kinds of delicacies here.  Even the juice brands here I've not found elsewhere and they are delicious.  The guys working behind the counter are always extremely pleasant and fun to deal with.  If ever you are unsure of something they're always willing to help, even allowing you to try out something before you make the purchase making your decision making easier.  Thumbs up to Dattilos.  Great place to grab a hoagie, real Italian deli, great bread, meats and other unique condiments.

We were here on a Friday night and enjoyed our time drinking,  having conversations,  observing other customers in the basement area. Plenty of eye candies that night. We spent at least 2 hours there. We will be back again. Good friendly service. You can actually go upstairs, they occupy the whole building, which I remember from previous visits.

Before heading back home from my Philly trip, I decided to stop at a cheesesteak spot that I have never tried before.  You pretty much cant go wrong with any cheesesteak in Philly, but I wanted to switch it up from my usual spots.  Where I was, this was close by and had excellent reviews.  I went simple and just got a standard cheesesteak with wiz and onions.  I must say, this was a delicious steak sandwich.  The meat was cooked perfectly and was very juicy.  The cheese was just the right amount.   The onions were a nice touch.  And I added a little bit of ketchup for additional flavor.  I ate the whole cheesesteak in one sitting.  Overall, I was very impressed and satisfied with this steak.  I would come back to try a different style steak sandwich,  as they offered many different kinds.

i was looking for some healthy spots in the nolibs area and this place was recommended to me!

overall, it was tasty but the meat was a bit chewy and it wasnt cheap!
for $40 we got a kebab salad, kebab entree and a hummus w/ pita

the hummus and pita was delicious! i wish the pita was warm but the hummus was delicious

i got the lamb and beef kebab. the beef was super chewy and i ended up not eating them but the lamb was decent, not as chewy as the beef luckily. the salad was decent, nothing crazy but a good assortment of veg (cucumber, tomato, red onion) the vinagrette dressing was tasty!

i tried my husband's chicken and lamb entree and it was good. the side salad in the entree is a little sad though 

i would maybe come back for the hummus but definitely ordering something else next time, a meat that's less chewy!

Was craving Korean food, so we ordered some takeout from Buk Chon, as the reviews looked promising. 

We ordered our usual go-to dishes, a soft tofu stew and the Jap-Chae. The order came with banchan, packed in three condiment sauce cups, one of the saddest looking and most disappointing banchan I've ever had.

The tofu stew and the Jap-Chae were standard. The tofu stew could use a little more spice though.

I recently had my first ever experience at Fiorella and it was incredible! Although they only had outside dining available and limited seating, they have a really nice outdoor setup that doesn't take away from the experience. I would recommend getting a reservation ahead of time.  The food was delicious, drinks were yummy and the staff was very attentive and great at providing recommendations.

Although my nails and feet turned out okay. The woman who did them wasn't consistent with applying produts and massaging.  What I mean by that is that one arm, hand and foot was massaged better and longer than the other/ had more or less product applied to it!  I also felt like she was rushing to service  me.(She also didn't even out the shape of my 2 big toes. So that they were identical.) Which I couldn't understand because they weren't packed! And even if they were, that not an excuse to shorthand a customer! She also kept slapping away my fingers as she was going over each one which I personally feel is very rude and annoying to say the least. And she didn't scrub my feet smooth. Which is saying a lot seeing as how there was barely any roughness to them! This was my first time coming, and it might be my last. It cost too much money for something as simple as a manicure and pedicure these days. To have received this type of service!

Consistently good food. Their weekend brunch is their specialty in my opinion. The eggs benedict and chicken and waffles are outstanding. Cocktails are tasty too.  Staff is always friendly and courteous.

First time at this place and was extremely happy with it.  Service and staff were excellent, quick, friendly and knowledgeable about the menu.  If you like middle eastern-Israeli food you will love this restaurant.  Salatin-Hummis plate has diverse offerings that are sure to please.  I had the grilled beef lamb entree, excellent flavor but a little to salty.

Great place to see a movie. The theater is very clean, the lines move fast, and the bar and lounge are both very attractive. Compared to the AMC on Broad or in Cherry Hill this is paradise. The seats are comfortable, the restrooms are clean, and the concession lines are fast and efficient. I have been to five movies here so far and look forward to more as an AMC Stubs A List member.

Oh man, this place is so different from the chain in NYC.

The worker wasn't the friendliest, and just stared rather than greeting us? Confused. We ordered the Mango Kakigori ($8.50). Not worth at all! I understand if they're practicing COVID precautions, their utensils are disposable, but it's just so sad to see the dessert just given in a SMALL plastic bowl. The ice was good and fruity, but the syrup was strong and it just tasted like artificial mango syrup. The mango fruits they provided were also just canned mangoes, although I like the pop mango. 

This was sadly not it and a ripoff.

Just purchased this print from Pretty Green Terrariums. Wonderful little place my friend and I stumbled upon. Staff was friendly and very helpful. He told us he plants all the terrariums himself. So impressive! Will definitely be visiting again!
Food was subpar for what was supposed to be a 5-Star restaurant.  Contract parking attendant said the Ford Explorer was oversized and took me for an extra $7!  Avoid this place...

I came here for happy and I was impressed with the food and service here. The wait staff was really kind and accommodating. We made reservations via phone and was greeted very kindly. We asked about bringing a dog and was told that it was okay to bring. They even gave him a bowl

Decided to try the place out because of the great reviews. Food was good! However, I'm so disapointed and amazed how uncofortable and unwelcomed the bartender made us feel. As we arrived we were directed to seat at one of the hight tops, we didnt get the time to sit and take our coats off he already asked us what we want to drink, we asked for a couple of minutes and that set him off to roll his eyes and just walk away! You're a grown man, really? Then he just talked shit about us to his coworkers while staribg at us.. what a great customer service! Finally, I went to the bar to irder after a few minutes he finally decided to take my order I was a bartender for over 10 years now I'm a manager at a big establishment I swear I have never spoken to any of my guests in a manner I was spoken to by this unplesant man! Throughout the visit he touched every table at the restaurant but ours and when I approached the bar he literally turned around and pretended  tp not see me! NEVER COMING BACK AGAIN I'll choose Maggies every single time. I really hope the owner reads this as I was hoping to speak with them in person.

Much improved over the years and in winter my teen enjoys the River Rink.

Lots to see and do in summer, too.
Famous for Fireworks (and crowds) on July 4th.

It was the best of meals, it was the worst of meals.  We had a 7 PM Sunday reservation for my wife's birthday dinner.  THE BEST:  As on our prior visit, the food was uniformly excellent - we had edamame dumplings and tuna pizza for appetizers, and pad thai (without the shrimp) and chicken in plum sauce (with tofu substituted for chicken) for entrees.  All of it was really tasty, and the entree portions were generous.  THE OK:  The menu included NO vegetarian entrees.  The server specifically mentioned that vegie substitutions were available for the two entrees we ended up ordering, but this is 2021 and any decent restaurant should have at least a few flesh-free entrees on the menu.  After an initial lapse (possibly just an innocent miscommunication), the server was fairly attentive.  THE WORST:  We asked to be seated in the quietest possible location, which the hostess claimed was the balcony.  Nonetheless, even there we were totally overwhelmed with loud, throbbing, pulsating music, and had to practically yell at each other across the table to be heard.  And the lighting was so minimal it was difficult to read the menu without using our phones for flashlights.  This is not the auditory or visual environment we want when we splurge on expensive dinners, and so we will not return to Buddakan.

Great food, great price. I have never been to/or eaten Peruvian food so it was a great change. Awesome service, and SUPER helpful as we didn't know what to get since menu was so large and had dishes we never heard of. Also got to try Peruvian wine which was different and great!

This is not your zen massage. There are no frou frou candles or your choice of scented massage oils. Instead, they are fairly bare rooms--and great sports/deep tissue massages.
It may take some time to find the therapist whose technique works with what you want--but I've found a few that I love. 
Yes, it's a bit frustrating to have to wait outside, and to climb 4 flights of stairs. 
I've been a member for 6 months. It's definitely a huge cost savings if you go even more than 4 times a year of 60 minute massages.
I leave feeling a bit taller and stretched out, and feeling like my muscles recovered a bit better!

I ordered through Uber eats. My peppersteak platter was $15.75 and i ordered a $4.50 side of this macaroni and cheese that's raved about on Instagram. I wanted to try this place and I was sharing the food with my niece so I didn't concern myself with the price thinking there would be more than enough food. The food wasn't bad at all, but if you're going to charge so much for a platter I think you should specify the size of the platter. Had I known I would receive a small platter I certainly would've reconsidered!

This spot was so great, located right in center city with a really nice outdoor seating option. For lunch I got the dandelion salad and opted to add grilled chicken into it (you could also add salmon). The salad was perfect for a summer day out (mixed greens, avocado, cucumbers, and a delicious light dressing). The only downside of this place was that the menu was slightly limited!

I would never recommend anyone to use this legal service even if it cost $1.00. I started my legal service around October 20, 2020. I paid $2045.00 for a "simple" divorce through PayPal on October 22, 2020. Of course everything seemed good and normal because they were getting my money. After a few weeks to a month, I received a phone call from his secretary followed up with paperwork I needed to fill out and return. After months went by and now into 2021, I called and followed up with "what's going on?". They say, I need more paperwork filled out and to send it back. Did that and now we're into almost a year later, no new progress. Secretary says, I need to go to center city or call family court to get the withdrawal. I go downtown to find out that my legal center never filed my divorce through family court nor was his info in my files as my representative and I would have to file again with legal aid on Tuesday or Thursday 9:30-12:30pm. Ugh.... I've been in center 3 times in Thursday's paying at least $33.00 for parking each day. Now my legal service as not answered any of my phone calls or emails and I sent several. Never again. Now I can't get my money back, I got scammed and they wasted my time.

Philadelphia never ceases to disappoint. This is # 1 or 2 on most lists. Ha! Let me first say I gave one star for the quality. The meat is very good quality stuff. I gave the second star for the bread. The bread is absolutely PERFECT hoagie bread for cheesesteak. But that's all the good I can say. The steak is horribly bland. So what you get is a great roll soaked with beef that tastes like warm water. No salt. No pepper. Not a drop of sear. Nothing. This is a bland tasteless fail. It's a terrible fail, because the quality is there, the technique is not. To date, no famous Philadelphia cheesesteak has lived up to the hype. You will get better cheesteak at any Jersey Mike's than the "best" places in Philadelphia.

I was with an employee for about 25 to 30 minutes asking him about all of the tufted headboard beds and their prices. I can't remember his name I think it had a V in it?  He was helpful and attentive all throughout, but as soon as I told him I was thinking of ordering online as I was not decided on which bed to get and needed to talk it over with my family all of a sudden he became so rude. He handed me his card and stormed off saying "Well if you order it online I don't get paid and I've already spent all this time with you." I was shocked at the complete 180 his personality did finding out his kindness was just a front to get my money. Then on the way out as my father and I attempted to say goodbye to him he refused to make eye contact or say anything and an employee he was venting was the only one courteous enough to say anything. The worst part is I was attempting to find out how I could give him the service online for helping me out but he completely ruined that for himself. I will be giving my money to maybe the employee who did acknowledge me or the Exton, PA location, extremely unprofessional and off-putting. No other store, Apple, Nordstroms, no where do they act this way if your not ready to make a HUGE purchase off a whim.
Stumbled upon this place and will be going back. Food is pretty elevated for a brewery! Had duck hush puppies for that were soooo good

The atmosphere is great. You feel as if you are in an upscale restaurant in Mexico City. The waitstaff is knowledgeable and polite. Restaurant follow covid-19 guidelines completely. The drinks are good and filled with tequila. Highlight to eat or try- Chips & Salsa, Queso Fundido, Salsa Tequilas with shimp, Enchiladas Playa, and Molcajete. Will be back to try more dishes at this lovely restaurant. Best Mexican in Philly.

No wait at 5:30 pm on a Saturday evening for a group of 4. We were seated promptly after the host took our temperatures. The booths have plastic separators between tables, and from what I saw, most of the restaurant was full. 3 of us got the tomato oxtail soup base, 1 had the original milky broth. I've tried both and I would say they are equally good, it just depends on what kind of mood you're in. Our server, Quynh, was very attentive and polite. 10/10 service and of course, the food was amazing. I liked the ponzu dipping sauce they provided, although it is a little different from other hotpot places that are more Chinese style with a variety of sauces like sesame, soy sauce, etc. Here at Chubby Cattle, they provide a ponzu sauce with a variety of toppings, including cilantro, green onion, chili, and garlic. The ponzu sauce paired perfectly with the meat (perfectly tender and nicely fatty without being too much) and other veggies. Overall, I think Chubby Cattle was wonderful (the terrarium light fixtures were a nice touch) and I will definitely be back again.

I would have taken a picture of my platter, but I wolfed it down too fast! I had the fish, eggs and Grits platter. Scrambled eggs with cheese where perfect, fluffy and delicious, enormous piece of crispy flounder fried to perfection and a generous portion of buttery grits! Perfect, exactly what I wanted! Will definitely order from here again!!!

I had a horrible exchange this morning with a cashier at the 3313 Wharton st Phila store Dunkin' Donuts. I simply ordered a grill cheese sandwich and ask for bacon on it. While ordering she was rushing me saying do you want ham do you want this I said one second I would like to have the sweet black pepper bacon. She then went on to say that you can't have that. I said well why not I should be able to have whatever I can pay for and I also ordered this all the time from other Dunkin' Donuts. So she said to me who do you think you're talking to and I thought wow what a horrible exchange. I ask for a manager she said yeah I'll get a manager the manager then proceeded to take my order and said so they'll be a little extra for the bacon I said not a problem I'm sure I can afford it I just don't understand why your agent told me I couldn't have whatever I wanted to order. I have never been spoken to like this when I'm spending my money and I don't believe that anything was done. So I did not take this order, I wasn't sure what would be safe to consume. Additionally I was in the drive-through for such a long time and during Covid you would think people would be understanding and even more accommodating. I hope this response to get some traction,Now I am very busy and I don't have time to do these reviews but this had to be submitted the Philadelphia grays ferry location I will never go there again.

Breakfast was really good  had the Eggs Benedict and the andouille breakfast hash eggs were cooked perfect and food was outstanding service could be a little warmer but all in all very good and is some of the best breakfast I've had in philly

I've been here once a while ago got a sandwich to go and after a half hour ride home it was ok but I knew that was because of the travel. Well I had a strong urge on Saturday to make the ride and this time I ate it "the spicy porker" in my car in front of the store and it was orgasmic it exceeded my lofty expectations by far! We're talking bucket list here in the bucket list list of culinary delight!

Westy's is my FAVORITE bar in Philadelphia!! So happy it opened back up! It's so safe inside, staff wearing masks and tables spread apart for social distancing, overall I was very impressed with their commitment to good service! The bartenders and staff were friendly, the food was PHENOMENAL, I would recommend this place to anyone. Love Westys!!

Wow, probably the largest sandwich I have ever had in my life! No wonder it costs almost $20! 

Ordered the pastrami sandwich and there was so much meat! It was actually a little too much meat in proportion to the veggies and bread. Plan on only being able to eat only one half of one of these sandwiches in one sitting. 

The meat itself wasn't anything spectacular, but maybe that was due to the overabundance. After a few bites, you get tired/bored of eating a big chunk of meat with not enough of the other ingredients.

I love our produce, meat, egg, and bread shares, especially during COVID when the grocery stores are sometimes lacking! Philly Foodworks has super responsive customer service, an extensive online market selection, tons of pickup locations + delivery, unique and unexpected options, and the flexible ability to swap out items I won't eat and/or skip weeks is a dream.

Really impressed with this place! The host was amazing, very accommodating and genuinely helpful. Nikki was our server the energy and service she provided was impeccable! She's def one off the best servers I have ever had! Loved the vibe, drinks and music. The whole place I highly recommended! Felt extremely welcomed and the whole place is a vibe, don't hesitate to come here!!!!

I visited the Target location at 4000 Monument Road to return a gift my son received for his birthday Sat. His grandma purchased him a car seat however it wasn't safety equipped so I was returning the chair to get a more secure one. I was told they didn't know why I couldn't return without a receipt. I explained that it was gift and a fist receipt wasn't provided. The cashier than told me "she didn't know why I wasn't able to return without a receipt" I called customer services and was advised that the item could be return however I would have to get someone else to do it. I don't recall returning without a receipt because I always use my Target card. The principal about the situation is how rude PAULETTE WAS. She told me she was a manager when I asked to speak to one Bieber another employee there advised she was a "front end lead". She slammed my id and Corp number on the counter I asked her to place it in my hand like I placed  it hers. She than advised that I didn't give it to her so she's not picking it up. She walked off leaving my other item on the counter and never returned. The original cashier returned and skipped right over me asked nice and politely to the Caucasian guy "how can I help you thanked him for his patience but never said another word as if I wasn't standing there. I understand many people have it set in their heads that "BLACKS ARE GHETTO AND STEAL" but everyone isn't like that. I work just like they do. On top of me spending so much money there on a reg. But I do know Target lost me as a customer and if his grandmother didn't live out of town I would tell her to get her money back. I will be boycotting Target until their employees know how to treat their customers.

Dr. Wolgin and his staff are wonderful. They are professional, kind and most importantly competent.  
Thank you for being a bright light in Philadelphias medical community.

It just opened this morning and we got a breakfast sandwich, a hazelnut latte and a few of their little cakes. The chocolate cake and the coffee/chocolate cakes are decadent and delicious and the latte was light and delicious. Highly recommend!

Oh my God, Lucky's Last Chance is actually pretty darn cool. Can't wait to try every single thing off the menu here. The menu is really good, so many very good choices, I had to go with Onion Strings, and it was amazing. The crew is definitely a highlight of this place because they are always quick, courteous, and provide service with a smile! Totally returning here again for more because one time is just not enough.

Doggie VIP is great! My dog Chase was very nervous at first and Victoria was amazing with him. They gradually introduced him to other calm dogs and were so patient with him as he got acclimated. After that he loved his time and playing with all his new dog friends. I highly recommend Doggie VIP Philly !!

You all know by now that I'm very particular when it comes to my nails. I had found the perfect salon but moved in the last year and had the daunting task of finding a new one. I tried a few locally and was consistently disappointed. That's when a friend recommended Modish so I figured I had nothing to lose. 

The salon is gorgeous. Clean, neat, and beautiful. You can walk in but they are busy so I prefer to make an appointment. Minh is always at the desk to greet you. He's friendly and wants you to have the best experience possible. He keeps things moving in the salon and always offers a drink. Tammy is my nail girl. She's sweet, takes her time and she makes sure I like what she is doing. She helps me pick a color and always asks if I like it before completing the rest of my hand. I always get the dip powder and am completely satisfied. They last three weeks but I could definitely go longer if it wasn't for my nails growing out. I am so happy my hunt for a new nail salon is over. And I'm so happy I found Modish.

Honestly the brisket was delicious but bread was a little bit dry, not quite stale but they could have at least toasted it with butter or something, I felt like the ratio was a little off between meat and bread. 

That being said I have had their bbq in the past and the other items definitely slap, looking forward to trying again

The best thing was the salad. I must say the silver plastic ware I was impressive, but as you can see snapped right in half. Sort of representation of the entire meal. Looks awesome, not worth half the money.  Only gave them three stars because chocolate mousse with Cohl and the salad was all right. Let me see the lobster meat wasn't bad it was just completely unseasoned.  Would never do it again!  If Capital Grille had a delivery platform, Iwould never had been disloyal.

I'm jumping right in... Best thing on the menu is the Jerk Chicken!  The Curry Goat is ok..needs more seasoning!
The sides need help-Period!

We all have watch every food rescue type of show where the expert states 'focus on what you are good at and get rid of the rest'!  The Mac and cheese (shells..is a joke-not cheesy at all..straight out of a box ; the rice and beans need seasoning; the cabbage was the best..keeper)!

Friendly staff and good portions for the price..if I could give 3.5 stars I would for the things just mentioned!

Not sure I would try again when there are so many other good food options in the area!

The Mecca of Philly cheesesteaks!!! This is where the story of creating a Philly cheesesteak started!! These cheesesteaks are some of the best I've ever had!! I like my Cheesesteak with onions and cheese whiz! The provolone is a popular pick too! The fries are better at Pats than Geno's! There are two lines; one for ordering a cheesesteak and the other for ordering drinks or french fries. This is one of my favorite things to hit in Philly everytime I am there!!

This place was amazing. I loved seeing Van Gogh sunflower painting. It was so beautiful to see it again person. I loved all the different artwork they had. I did get lost in the museum but it was still fun lol. I was a bit disappointed that I couldn't see the Rocky Steps though.
I've been waiting for some perfect BBQ since I moved up here from Texas six years ago. Got the brisket, potato salad and mac cheese. GRADE A+ BBQ!!! The brisket melts in your mouth. Sooooo good!!

I once thought Tony Luke's was worthy of being above the "tourist trap" designation. 

It had been a while since I've been here. I gave them a shot today. 

Whatever was not true then may be true now. 

This wasn't a bad cheesesteak. There's nothing wrong with it. But I've had a lot of different cheesesteaks in town since I last had an original Tony Luke. 

And now I'm noticing that the beef flavor just doesn't sit the same way here as other places. I'm noticing that it seems saltier with the cheese. I'm noticing that the flavors don't seem to marry as well as other places. I'm noticing that it seems to be a little greasier than others. 

There's nothing wrong with Tony Luke's. They have many great sandwiches. The rolls are wonderful. 

But as of today, they've fallen out of my top 10 in the city. There's newer places and classic places just doing this sandwich better right now. 

1. Angelo's 
2. John's 
3. Woodrow's 
4. Oh Brother 
5. Dalessandro's 
6. Philip's 
7. Ace of Steaks 
8. Max's 
9. Joe's 
10. Gooey Louie's

Honorable mentions: 
- Jim's 
- Steve's 
- Tony Luke's 
- Ishkabibble's 
- Pat's

If I could write Murph's a million 5-star reviews, I would. I've said it once and I'll say it again - Murph's is the best Italian food in Philadelphia. Came during covid for outdoor dining - they have a cute little tent out front that is open on multiple sides (not one of those unsafe outdoor-indoor structures) and heat lamps to keep you warm.

We started with mussels au gratin and fried mozzarella (they were sadly out of fried burrata). The mussels were a surprisingly large portion, and the fried mozz was clearly fresh/better quality than what you normally think of when you order this app.

For the main course, we ordered a rack of lamb and tagliatelle with filet to share. Both were insanely delicious. If you like lamb, definitely try theirs - it's only $25 for a full rack and side of pasta. We easily had two extra meals of leftovers to take home.

The mains were a little delayed to come out, so Murph's kindly gave us dessert on the house - we had the creme brulee cheesecake and lemon marcapone cake. You can't go wrong with either.

While waiting for a table, I had a Morrison Mule and Bourbon Spritz. I would... you guessed it - recommend both. Not sure if they're still doing this, but they gave me the drink in a plastic cup so I could wait outside with it!

They're also doing takeout during the pandemic, so definitely make sure to take advantage of it while you can!! They're cash only but their prices are so affordable. If you want to see their latest menu and specials, make sure to check out their instagram!
The team at Opportunity Barks clearly care about every pup and their families. They take this work seriously while having So Much Fun!

Such a cute, intimate spot. Great addition to Germantown! I tried ALL of the ciders. Most of the are drier but the raspberry (seasonal) is on the sweet side. I really enjoyed the ginger & blood orange. The pies are fantastic! I tried the Route 23 & Smoky-Spicy Shroom. They were great, but phenomenal when I ate them together. This is a cute spot for a meetup with friends or a casual date. I also got to meet the owner Stephanie who is kind & delightful. Definitely check this place out if you're in the neighborhood or love cider!

Wow, Gianfranco Pizza Rustica was simply amazing. I'm so glad to be here and the environment is so pretty. Terrific food, Chicken Ranch Pizza was excellent without a doubt. This Chicken Ranch Pizza was prepared just perfectly. The crew was excellent, literally everyone. I am so happy with this place.

Parking: Economy parking remains closed even though the airport has resumed many flights. If you want to know why there's no space in Garage B or C, check here first on your way to the airport: https://philapark.org/airport-parking/
That has 15 minute updates on spaces available by garage so you won't circle in vain looking for a spot when you should be getting to TSA. 
I wound up in Garage A this trip which was OK outbound with a walk, though my arriving flight came back all the way to F. So I got exercise. There is a shuttle that goes from F to other terminals (C and A). 

Security: TSA was pretty quick. Covid or not, it's the same rules as before, laptop and large electronics out, shoes/belts/coats/hats off, pockets empty. Liquid rules still in effect. 

Shopping/Food: Fewer choices and limited hours. I waited til I got to my destination to eat. 

Covid: Seating areas still have social distancing stickers. Masks required.

Have only had food to go and only been here once, so a bit tentative but here are my thoughts. Overall food is more on the balanced and less of the extreme spice compared with the older Circles, and some other places in the city. This is definitely on the milder end and is probably on par with ratchada or even a bit milder than that.

More traditional Thai cuisine (in terms of what's typically found in the U.S.) compared with Kayala, which is Southern Thai specifically.

Even though I wouldn't mind more spice, the food is quite balanced from a taste standpoint. Have had a particularly good luck with the salads, as well as the pad Thai and the basil noodles with chicken.

Delicious! Been here a bunch of times never had any issues. Staff always friendly. Great rewards app you get a free platter for your birthday but they give you plenty of time to use it. Combo platter is my go to. Love the sauces. Extra White & Hot. Try the bbq also for a different taste. Fries are tasty.  Highly recommend.

Won't be back!! The general  toast chicken isn't consistent AT ALL!! 
The first time it was delicious. The second time it was dry and super breaded, I have them another try and it was WORST! I will not be back. I called and told them and it still was WRONG. Just ewwwww. So much liquid and not yummy liquid

after all my heads of hearing how amazing monks beer program was, i finally went. & i wasn't really blown away. the first beer on tap was allagash white lol, like why? they had a few good beers but i was under the impression it would be the best of the best and all hard to find stuff.

worst company of all-time, in all of history. my internet doesn't work just being one room away from the signal, constantly goes in and out. The service technicians don't show up half the time, and it's intentional. Good luck getting someone to show up. I'd rather have no internet at all than comcast. waste of time, and pointless frustration.

Came here to get my fingerprints done for clearances and ended up having to come TWICE to get them redone. I've gotten my prints done ~10 times due to the nature of my job and volunteering, but my prints have NEVER been rejected at the other 9 locations I've been to. Only have they been rejected here, where they clearly don't care to do it right the first time.

I get it, it's covid, they probably want me out of there asap. But hey, if the computer clearly says print not wide enough, or insufficient tips, then just redo them instead of hitting continue so you don't have to make me return to contaminate your store again!  When I saw the lady doing a sloppy job even the second time, I mentioned my first prints were rejected because they weren't clear, and she said well, you get to try 3 times. 
This place clearly doesn't care about wasting your time and forcing you to continue coming back. 

Long story short - DO NOT COME HERE TO GET YOUR FINGERPRINT DONE UNLESS YOU WANT TO WASTE TIME GETTING THEM REDONE AND/OR YOU WANT TO MISS YOUR DEADLINE.

UPDATE AFTER DAVID's COMMENT:
I understand the importance of keeping everyone safe during COVID and having that effect the amenity spaces t some capacity. I would like to make something clear that I left out in my previous review: I specifically asked what the elevator situation was after seeing reviews, and they said with Covid, "they're allowing 5 people in at a time". I have the email to prove it. Turns out it was only 2 people, and still is, with more than 600 people living in the building. The elevators do not "work properly" for the population of people living here, when most of the time you have to wait 20 minutes for an elevator up or down. I also specifically asked about construction, as I knew I was going to be working from home, and they lied about that as well and said they were unaware of the start date after it started 2 weeks post me moving in. Again, really urge you to find another building if you're reading these reviews! This place is not worth it. 

UPDATE AFTER 9 MONTHS OF LIVING HERE:
The construction is finally finished but this building is NOT worth it. We have an amazing view of Center City - but I would trade that + anything else to not have to wait for an elevator for 20+ minutes. My boyfriend and I literally don't even go out during lunch because we are afraid we will spend 40 minutes waiting for an elevator and waste 40/60 min of our lunch break. The fire alarm goes off multiple times a month. The amenities are still closed to anyone other than the guests, even the outdoor roof deck due to COVID. The management does not care about you as soon as you sign and are completely unapologetic for mistakes made on their part. 

If you're planning on moving any time soon, pick ANY other building. We have maintenance in here every other week due to something new breaking. Our AC unit literally does not work, yet we are charged for amenities at a higher rate than any other building in center city (trust me, I've done my research). Haven't even submitted a maintenance request because maintenance never seems to fix anything., will schedule with you and then not show up, and then show up RANDOMLY with no warning and get mad when you say you're working from home and can't have them making noise at 11 am on a Tuesday. I asked them to fix the fan in our bathroom as a lot of moisture was accumulating, and he said he, "could replace it so it would make less noise, but the fans don't work and it's functionality won't change". They openly admit their appliances don't work and don't do anything about it! As I said below, the only plus side of this building is the staff at the front desk - they're awesome and really friendly. We are moving to a new building in center city two months prior to our lease ending and paying double the rent (finishing out our lease with 1500 Locust as well as paying for the new building) just to get out of here. 

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Just moved into the building on July 1. It's in a great location and seems to have great amenities - though the gym is not open due to COVID19. Disappointed with the communication of the building - there is some sort of construction project going on that sounds as though someone is drilling INSIDE your apartment. I was not made aware of this when I signed my lease. I called the leasing office, asking what was going on, and their answer was that they are having something done to the building and it normally takes about 2 1/2 months. Shouldn't people that are going to be affected by the noise be notified - especially with COVID19 and 90% of the population working from home? Apparently not. This is a huge problem for anyone that is working from home, or simply wants some peace and quiet when they're in their apartment. I chose this building because I expected it to be quiet and well managed and have been extremely disappointed in that regard so far.

Also, some of the amenities such as the large outdoor rooftop is restricted to resident's only due to COVID19. When I had asked the concierge downstairs, they said that was only the case because of the July 4 weekend, and any other day, as long as it wasn't a large group, others were allowed to join you on the outdoor rooftop. I went to sit outside with my boyfriend and was confronted by a man that was rude and not friendly stating that "NO ONE OTHER THAN A RESIDENT CAN BE UP HERE". That's fine, and given the circumstances I understand - but have your staff on the same page and not giving out conflicting information.

Plus side is that though the information they give out conflicts that of other staff members, the concierge downstairs are very helpful and nice.

I love this spot! I took my mom here on one of the coldest nights of the year (oops!) but was so mesmerized by the little heated huts that I had to try it out. Each hut has two floor heaters so it's really not that cold, especially if you don't mind keeping your coat on. The food was delicious as well. We started off with the Toma Celena Hygee Board, which did not disappoint. I ordered the fried chicken bites and french fries, paired with the Seasonal Punch. Even though it was tasty, I highly recommend ordering their warm cocktails in the winter months though, especially if you're eating outside. My mom had the mulled wine and lasagna. Great service and felt totally safe. Hope to visit again soon!

We stopped in around 10am on a Sunday. Several people waiting outside. We walked in and ordered 2 toasted bagels with cc. They asked us to wait outside and would call our names. After 15 min and people before us still waiting, I went inside to ask about our order. Several orders were sitting there with ours being one of them now cold.  Bagels were alright but customer service has several opportunities for improvement.

Located on 9th Street in the Italian Market.
A vegan red that sits right next to the House of Pork.
Lol! I was very surprised by how much that "chicken" cheesesteak was so good I didn't miss the meat.
It was fresh and flavorful! I will definitely be going back.

Just read they denied service to a Philadelphia Police Officer working the second half of a double shift, keeping us safe, simply because he is a LEO.
Word travels fast, Dunkin' Doughnuts, and my family will NEVER darken the door of one of your outlets again.  Truth be told, I always thought your food and coffe were garbage to begin with, but now I have an Ace card to stop anyone else in my family from patronizing your loathesome establishment.

OMG! I was looking for a late night taco spot to get some good food that would be able to cater to different dietary restrictions And this place hit the mark. We ordered chicken quesadillas, mushroom tacos, chicken tacos, and an order of guacamole and chips and everything was just fantastic! The food was fresh the staff was nice and I overall had a good takeout ordering experience. If you're planning to go make sure you order the guacamole it's so worth it and the prices were pretty average as well. I will definitely visit again especially once were off of quarantine.

Ordered delivery recently and was generally underwhelmed. I've ordered from here in years past and the food has always been pretty good. The best in Philly? Not close. But a decent option that will suffice. The restaurant is nice and not like those fast food corner spots you often find in the city. 
Not sure if it is due to the pandemic but our food simply wasn't delicious. We ordered General Tso chicken, shrimp with noodles and duck stir fry. None of it was great. The meat was dry and to sweet. Flavors lacked complexity which we usually look forward to in Chinese food. Maybe I am spoiled by my favorite Chinese food place in DC. 
Needless to say, we won't be ordering from here again. I'll take my chances with picking up from father away if the food will taste better.

Never again! As if moving isn't stressful enough especially when you're moving out of state. Uhual was happy to add to that stress.
Reserved a truck over a month in advance at this location. Got a call the day before our move that the location we preferred didn't have any trucks and we would have to drive 45 minutes away to another location. Frustrating, but okay. Might have been less frustrating if the people working here and the regional office didn't have "it is what it is" attitude.
Luckily we have a car so we will drive 45 minutes out of the way, no problem. Let's be clear though, there are a lot of people in the city that don't own cars and rely on a quick Uber ride or public transportation. If I had to dish out money for a 45 minute Uber right the day of moving I'd be even more pissed.
So we call the next location to confirm only to find their phones aren't in service. So then we call uhual customer service to see if they can confirm the pickup - nope. Zero help - "not sure what to tell ya. Just wait for them to call you to confirm". We are driving out of state - not what I want to hear.
Well, we finally got through to Uhual in Media hours later to hear "we don't know why they told you to come here. We don't have any trucks available." LOL (let me be clear - this was the nicest person working for uhual - my issue is not with this location).
So, I called Budget even though it said they were sold out of everything online, but with much better customer service they were able to find us a truck last minute. They had much better communication which is what you want when you're dishing out $600+ and moving in less than 24 hours.
I will never use uhual again. Horrible communication and terrible customer service. People here will roll their eyes and say "well what do you want me to do about it" - I don't know? Honor a reservation from over a month ago? BYE!

I ordered takeout a few months ago and had a great experience. Tonight I ordered takeout again and got about have of the serving size that I received previously - super frustrating.  

The food tastes good, but why am I overpaying first half the portion size I can get somewhere else?
Went tonight for restaurant week! Great food, great service! Tess was our server! So nice & accomadating! Really cool vibe!! Try it!

This is just a cool experience from start to finish. When you arrive to the restaurant, you walk down a flight of steps, as the restaurant is underground! Walking down the hallway into the main room, everything just screams old-school Italian (colors, wall paper, paintings, furniture, texture.) 

This is a great place for summer or fall dinner - just an extremely cozy atmosphere. 

Everything on their menu is solid, but a really cool feature is that they bring the specials out on a cart to showcase to you.

So we called ahead to see if dine in was available and drove almost 45 minutes to come here at Dim Sum. We got here around 8:20pm and they told us they won't serve us since they are really busy with online orders. The person we spoke to was absolutely rude and turned us away. We tired explaining to him that we called ahead twice and both times they said to come by but he wasn't having it. I will never come to this place ever again . This was an absolute embarrassment.

Got take out from here last weekend during the time of COVID. Food was excellent! Service was a bit slow but that was just because they were super busy. 

Called to place an order for dinner for take out on a Saturday. Called by 5 or so and they were already out of Satay and goat which was sad! Ordered a Nasi campur with beef randang and collard greens and cendol. A hefty helping of food for not much money at all! Beef was super tender and delicious. Mix of spices was great. The collard greens came in coconut curry/sauce and were great. Tender and not bitter at all. Everything was also not super salty. The cendol was different but delicious as well. Nice mix of flavors and not super sweet like bubble tea. Straw they gave with it was way to small to eat the little jellies at the bottom. 

Service was a bit spotty. When I went to pick up the food there were at least 10 people waiting outside. No one would answer the door if you knocked or answer the phone if you call. Someone finally came out 10min later and gave me my food. They were super busy (she actually said they were unable to take any further orders at the time) but it would have been nice if they had a better system, since it seems like its always like this. 

Excellent Indonesian food (for sure the best I've had in philly). Service was a bit eh, but I'm glad they're staying busy during COVID. Check them out for sure!

We purchased city pass and decided to give this zoo a try. We had prepaid parking for the garage - it was easy to just park and start walking. It's a less than 5 mins walk from garage to the zoo. We went for 10am slot where the garage had plentiful of parking spaces available. 

As soon as you enter there is restroom and a mobile rider rental. Restrooms were clean and almost around every few blocks which is very convenient. The animals in the zoo looked well fed. The only regret we had was many exhibits were closed.

This little hole in the wall is as grungy as it gets, but you won't find a better cheese steak in Filly, the term 'looks can be deceiving' definitely applies here. It's a working class establishment, that's why it's off the beaten path, but if you do something exceptional, who cares what the place looks like.

This was a surprise find.  We were just driving by this area when we decided to stop for a bite to eat.  We googled places to eat near our location, Yiro Yiro happened to come up.  We love greek food and decided to give this place a try.  Wow, it did not disappoint, Everything we had was delicious and fresh.   We had the chicken skewers, one with the spicy tzatziki sauce and the regular, both were amazing.  The chicken was tender and juicy.  The rice had nice flavor and was cooked to perfection as well as the grape leaves.  We will have to come back to this place and try the yogurt which looked delicious, we had no room for dessert being the platters were huge.  Can't wait to come back to this special little find.  Really would like to add the service and the people working at this place were super nice.

Yeah that pastrami sandwich is real good. At first when I ordered it and saw the small-ish pieces of bread they put down on the counter, I thought I would be disappointed. But they really layer on the meat, and the sandwich is huge. I ended up splitting the sandwich and it was flavorful, greasy, and delicious. I do wish there was some type of sauce to add to it, but I don't like mustard so that's my fault. I just had meat and cheese and it was delicious. Great flavor, big, meaty, and tasty. I don't even like sandwiches but I thoroughly enjoyed this one.
Cute and quaint spot for coffee and tea. We stopped here for a beverage break after a little tour of Philadelphia. The service was quick, and the drinks were good.

Just to preface: I am a bit of a snob when it comes to sushi. In an ideal world, omakase and nigiri all day everyday but COVID got a sister changing her ways. We dropped by for takeout and I realized that Vic is better as a roll place, not so much for sushi/nigiri/sashimi. We ordered the three roll special (Alaska, eel, and spicy tuna), a specialty roll I forgot but it featured white seaweed, and sashimi. The rolls were good but nothing spectacular - rice fell apart quickly, etc. They were affordable at $12-13 for 3 of them. The sashimi cuts were a let down (and IMO really tells you the quality of their fish selection and overall execution- even affordable places can have wonderful sashimi). It was clear that everything was previously frozen as there was a freezer taste to it, even the salmon, which was surprising. That said, it's a decent find but not one I plan to return to soon. Would I recommend? Maybe if you're a roll person, but not so much if you're a bit more advanced.

I had a corned beef reuben and it was really good.  The matzo ball soup was also really good, really strong, and it was just what the doctor ordered because it was cold and rainy outside and I was starting to come down with what turned out later to be pneumonia.

And, they have cel-ray!   That was probably the clincher for me as far as the fifth star goes.  Eating a sandwich this good without a cel-ray would be really sad.

For a long time, I said I was never giving a Jewish deli 5 stars unless it was as good as the original Goodman's on Elmora Avenue in Elizabeth, NJ (which no deli ever will be I'm quite sure).  But I decided that's not fair at all because it's an impossibly high standard to meet.

I sat at the counter and got great service from a very friendly guy who was on top of everything no matter how busy they got. 

As I've said in other reviews, the Jewish deli scene in NYC is pretty sad these days, especially in Manhattan, so I really appreciate a place that still cares and does it right.

I more or less stumbled upon Aldo Lamberti Trattoria in Philadelphia's international airport after a flight. During COVID-19 quite a few options are closed so I decided to get some food where I could before my next flight. I'm sure glad I did.

I was skeptical at the food at first, as it's airport food, however don't let that keep you away. The food is delicious and of really good quality. I have gotten some slices of pizza here, both cheese and veggie which were very good. I also have had a eggplant parm stack that was absolutely delicious. The eggplant is spot on. 

The line moves quickly and the people are nice. They have a sanitizing station as well as some condiments towards the end of the line. I absolutely will not hesitate to come here again.

Solid, locally owned spot with a killer three roll special deal.

Whenever you want sushi but don't want to break the bank getting it, Vic's is where to go. I've tried their spicy salmon, spicy tuna, shrimp tempura, Alaska (salmon and avocado), and regular salmon and tuna rolls and everything has been fresh and fantastic. They're fast and usually have everything ready for you in 20 minutes or less.

Limited indoor seating because it's a small place but great for pickup! No frills, clean, fresh, fast sushi.

This place books up fast! And now I can see why. My friends and I had a late night reservation. We had a table inside and felt very safe with dividers in between each table and the restaurant had an open concept.
First off drinks were pretty fantastic! I got the daily Puerto Rico punch (something about strawberry and passion fruit) very delicious. 
It was late night so we decided to try a bunch of different things. My friends who are vegan and vegetarian were so excited to try everything! We ended up getting the beef nachos, beef empanadas, Spanish meatballs with bread and yuca fries. I am not vegan and wasn't sure how the food will taste since I'm love meat but wow! I'm blown away at the flavors in each dish. My favorites had to be the beef empanadas (even though it's a bit pricey for 2 small empanadas) and the nachos. The meatballs were good too but the texture was a little weird for me.
My friends for the tres leches coconut cake and raspberry hazelnut dessert to go! I had a bite of the tres leches cake and it's divine! Yum def. Pricey for the food but def. Worth it especially for vegan/vegetarians!

Located in south Philly, John's Roast Pork has been a Philadelphia institution for the past 20 years. Established in 1930, this family-run restaurant is currently run by John Bucci Jr., the third generation owner. This restaurant is old school, only taking cash, and has strange hours so make sure it's open before making the drive. During COVID-19, customers have to call in advance to place their order. Because the restaurant is so famous, recognized by the James Beard Foundation in 2006 as an "American Classic," the process of calling to place your order is very hectic. Most of the time, they do not pick up their phone as the line is always busy. It can take over 20 attempts to finally reach a worker to place your order, but luckily, the hassle is worth it.

Although Roast Pork is in their name, they are just as famous for their cheesesteaks as they are for their roast pork sandwiches. I ordered their roast pork sandwich with spinach and sharp cheddar and their cheesesteak with white american cheese, the way John Bucci Jr. recommends. Firstly, both sandwiches were extremely fresh and were ready exactly at my assigned pick up time. For the roast pork, the sandwich was stuffed to the brim with surprisingly juicy and flavorful meat. I expected it to be much drier than it was. The sharp cheddar added a nice kick to the sandwich, and the spinach cut the fat of the meat well. The sesame seed was also excellent as the seeds provided a change to the otherwise monotonous texture of both sandwiches. Overall, this sandwich is quite excellent and really surprised me by how good it was. I personally believe it is worth the hype.

Now let's talk cheesesteak! This sandwich is jam packed with steak, onions, and cheese. There must have been at least five slices of cheese which is great for cheese lovers, but I personally think there was too much cheese. Although there is a lot of fried onions, they provide a nice sweetness that improves the overall flavor of the cheesesteak. This sandwich is really delicious, but compared to other Philadelphia cheesesteaks, it is on the heavier side. While the sandwich is quite good and is definitely a must try if you go on a cheesesteak tour, I much prefer the roast pork sandwich.

In conclusion, John's Roast Pork is a must try spot for any food lover visiting Philadelphia. If you go during the pandemic, the ordering process is a bit stressful and confusing, so I would recommend calling early and often until you reach the staff and place your order. Don't give up on calling them (as I almost did after many attempts) because the food and overall experience is worth it.

ASK FOR RYAN AS YOUR SERVER! He was so very nice and patient with us as we tried to figure out what we wanted to eat. The bread basket was dropped off as we sat down and the drinks were quick to arrive, as well as delicious! I got the Pampelmousse with the macaroni, which were both so good. Macaroni put me in a food coma! My friend got the cider drink with an omelette that she seemed to enjoy. As well. An amazing find on a rainy afternoon.
